cards.text: Last chapter of Numbers, friend. The family heads of the clan of Gilead, from the tribe of Manasseh, walk up to Moses and the leaders of Israel. They want to talk about their relative Zelophehad and the land the LORD said would be his family's inheritance.

cards.question: The family heads remind Moses what the LORD already commanded. Zelophehad's inheritance is to go to his ___.

cards.text: Then they lay out the problem, and it's a big "what if." I bet these men ran this scenario more times than I've checked an oven timer.

cards.question: If Zelophehad's daughters marry men from other tribes of Israel, what do the family heads say happens to their land?

answers.text: It is added to the tribe they marry into
It goes back to Moses to give out again
It is split up among the tribe of Levi

cards.text: Then they bring up the Jubilee. These men aren't planning for next week, friend. They're planning all the way out to the JUBILEE.

cards.question: The family heads say that when the Jubilee comes, the daughters' land will go back to the tribe of their fathers.

cards.text: Moses doesn't wing this one. He answers at the word of the LORD, and trust me, every time I wing a batch, the smoke alarm has something to say.

cards.question: What does Moses say about the concern the tribe of the sons of Joseph just raised?
Moses gives the LORD's command about Zelophehad's daughters. Who are the daughters allowed to marry?

answers.text: Anyone they please within their father's tribe
Only men that Moses chooses for them
Only men from the priestly tribe of Levi

cards.text: Then the rule gets BIGGER: no inheritance in Israel may be transferred from tribe to tribe. Every tribe's land stays PUT.

cards.question: Why can't an inheritance in Israel move from one tribe to another?

answers.text: Each Israelite keeps his fathers' tribal land
All the land belongs to the Levites
The lots can never be cast a second time

cards.question: This marriage rule is only for Zelophehad's daughters and no other daughter in Israel who inherits land.

cards.text: Moses says it one more time so nobody misses it: each tribe of Israel must keep its inheritance. Now it's up to Zelophehad's daughters.

cards.question: What do Zelophehad's daughters do with the command the LORD gave Moses?

answers.text: They do just as the LORD commanded
They ask Moses for a new ruling
They hand the land to their uncles

cards.text: Here are the sisters, by name: Mahlah, Tirzah, Hoglah, Milcah and Noah. And no, friend, not the Noah with the boat.

cards.question: The daughters of Zelophehad were married to ___ on their father's side.
After the daughters marry within the clans of Manasseh, their inheritance stays within the tribe of their father's clan.

cards.text: And that's how Numbers wraps up: these are the commandments and ordinances the LORD gave the Israelites through Moses on the plains of Moab, by the Jordan across from Jericho. The land stays with the family, friend, the same way this gold base stays with me.

findings.problem: Moses appears for the first time here, but the card doesn't say who he is (for example, Israel's leader).

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences. Story cards after the opening card are limited to 1 to 2.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The question calls the speakers "the tribe of the sons of Joseph," but card 1 only called them the clan of Gilead from the tribe of Manasseh. It dropped "one of the clans of Joseph" (36:1). The baker hasn't been told that these are the same people, so the question's context doesn't connect.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what.

findings.problem: Card 10 says "Every tribe's land stays PUT," which already gives the reason card 11 asks for (each Israelite keeps his fathers' tribal land). The right answer on card 11 just restates the setup and is easy to spot.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The question begins "This marriage rule," which points back to a rule on an earlier card the baker can no longer see. It should say what the rule is (marrying within a clan of their father's tribe).

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: "Moses says it one more time so nobody misses it" gives a reason for Moses repeating the rule. The text of 36:9 doesn't give one.

rule.text: Reasons: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: The right answer "They do just as the LORD commanded" repeats the question's wording ("the command the LORD gave Moses") and is the only answer that sounds like the Bible, so it stands out from the two wrong answers.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.
